decisionBox.changed: Position moves from endday's REDUCE to ADD, and the trigger is the single thing this desk's own lesson file said to wait for. The 14 August morning lesson reads: exhaustion needs a level that HOLDS when tested, not a big liquidation number - wait for the retest to succeed, then buy. That retest has now succeeded twice. First on the settle: the 22:00Z bar wicked 46.3 points through 62,846.3 and settled 36.4 points back above it, the first published line to survive its test in four sessions. Second on the overnight: price spent six and a half hours making a higher low at 62,991.0, 144.7 points clear of the line, without going back to touch it. Three secondary reads moved the same way. Positioning eased rather than built - the OKX long/short account ratio fell from 2.29 at 00:35Z to 2.25 at 07:00Z, off the 2.34 day high, which is the first decline in retail crowding since 13 August; funding eased from +0.00970% to +0.00871% for the 08:00Z settlement, so longs are paying less to hold; and forced selling has effectively stopped, with only $31,417 of long and $15,182 of short liquidations printed since 00:00Z against $5.25m long over the trailing 24 hours. On the timeframes, the 4H MACD histogram has crossed POSITIVE at +2.06 for the first time this week and the 1H histogram improved again to +37.13 from +33.68. What keeps this an ADD and not a bullish call is the daily chart, which has not changed at all: price sits below the 1D EMA20 at 63,889.02, the EMA50 at 64,414.50, the EMA100 at 66,510.36 and the EMA200 at 72,194.31, and the daily MACD histogram is -150.15 and widening. This is a low-conviction, direction-agnostic tranche into a long-term core at a level that held, sized accordingly, not a position taken on a trend that does not exist.

calibration.note: Endday's reduce line at 62,846.3 did NOT fire, and it was not even approached - the overnight low was 62,991.0, 144.7 points clear of it. The add line at 63,309.4 was never approached either; the overnight high was 63,189.1, short by 120.3 points, so its open-interest condition went untested for a third consecutive session. The trade is a small negative. Endday trimmed 18% of the spot book at 63,016.2, roughly 0.000285 BTC or 17.96 USDT of notional, and spot marks 91.0 points higher at 63,107.2, so the sold notional is offside by 0.144% or about 0.026 USDT, with a maximum favourable excursion of only 25.2 points to the 62,991.0 low and a maximum adverse excursion of 172.9 points to the 63,189.1 high. Rated no, and that makes twelve of the last fourteen. But the shape of the miss has changed in a way worth recording. Endday's stated reasoning was explicitly pre-emptive - it trimmed 169.9 points ABOVE its own invalidation rather than at it, precisely to correct the failure mode logged eleven times over. That correction WORKED as designed: the trade was wrong and it cost under three cents, because the exit was not standing in the liquidation cluster when the reversal came. Two consecutive sessions have now produced sub-three-cent misses on wrong calls. Sizing and placement discipline are converting bad calls into rounding errors, which is the only durable improvement in this file.
